children: Proposed 5.4 MW addition could take capacity to 14.6 MW, with funding planned through internal accruals and debt

E2E Networks on Monday, proposed expanding its computing infrastructure capacity by approximately 5.4 megawatts (MW) to support NVIDIA HGX B300 systems and other Blackwell graphics processing units (GPUs). The addition would increase its existing capacity of 9.2 MW to around 14.6 MW, an expansion of nearly 59 per cent if implemented in full.

The proposed expansion comes as the cloud computing company looks to address demand for GPU infrastructure and artificial intelligence (AI) computing services. E2E Networks plans to finance the capacity addition through a combination of internal accruals and debt, while the final investment and deployment timeline remain undisclosed.
Expansion To Support AI Training And Inference

The proposed infrastructure will support AI workloads across the development and deployment cycle, including large-scale foundation model training, post-training, production inference, agentic AI and multimodal applications, according to the company's press release.

E2E Networks said it was seeing demand from higher education and research institutions, foundation model developers, Indian and global AI-native startups, enterprises and public-sector programmes. It also highlighted demand for India-hosted computing infrastructure among organisations operating in regulated and data-sensitive environments.

Tarun Dua, founder and managing director of E2E Networks, said AI developers in India were moving beyond pilot projects towards training, fine-tuning and deploying models in production. He said the company was expanding its infrastructure in response to the demand it was seeing.
Investment And Deployment Timeline Remain Undisclosed

The company has not disclosed the total investment required for the proposed capacity addition or a fixed commissioning date. Its regulatory filing said the capital expenditure would depend on the infrastructure ultimately deployed, while the rollout would follow its deployment plan and anticipated demand for AI computing services.

The expansion is expected to be financed through a combination of internal accruals and debt. E2E Networks has also not specified the utilisation rate of its existing 9.2 MW capacity, saying the precise figure would need to be determined from its internal operational data.
